headline: The clinician said your burning after meals and when you lie down sounds like acid reflux, started you on lansoprazole, and asked to see you again in 8 weeks.

followUps.title: Start lansoprazole
followUps.detail: Take 30 mg once a day, about 30 minutes before breakfast.

followUps.title: Raise the head of your bed
followUps.detail: Raise it a few inches. The clinician said blocks under the bed legs work better than extra pillows.

followUps.title: Book your heartburn follow-up
followUps.detail: The clinician wants to see how your heartburn is doing.

followUps.title: Go to your appointment with Dr. Patel
followUps.detail: Dr. Patel will go over your heart scan (echo) report with you.

instructions.text: Take lansoprazole 30 mg once a day on an empty stomach, about 30 minutes before breakfast. It can take a few days to work fully.
Take lansoprazole, not omeprazole. Don't borrow Ruth's pills.
If you use an antacid tablet for heartburn, keep it a couple of hours apart from your other medicines.
Try not to eat in the 3 hours before bed.
Cut down on coffee, tomato sauces, and chocolate if you notice they bring on heartburn.
The clinician said ibuprofen and naproxen can irritate your stomach and make your heartburn and blood pressure worse.
Call sooner if you have trouble swallowing, vomit blood, see black stools, or get burning with exercise. These symptoms need to be checked quickly.

unchanged.text: You can still use antacid tablets if you get heartburn.
You can keep taking ramipril, atorvastatin, and vitamin D while you take lansoprazole.

openQuestions.text: Will you be able to lower your lansoprazole dose later? The clinician said not yet.
openQuestions.resolvesWhen: The goal is the lowest dose that controls your heartburn. No date was set for lowering it.

openQuestions.text: What did your heart scan show? The clinician said there was nothing urgent in the report.
openQuestions.resolvesWhen: Dr. Patel will review the report with you at your March appointment.
